question: What syllables and divine names form the body of this fourteen-syllabled mantra?
premises: The mantra includes the seed-syllables aiṃ and śrīṃ.
It addresses the daughter of Mekala and Narmadā.
It continues with the heart and so forth.
inference: The mantra is aiṃ, śrīṃ, to the daughter of Mekala, to Narmadā, followed by the heart and so forth.
plain_english: Aiṃ, śrīṃ, to the daughter of Mekala, to Narmadā, followed by the heart and so forth.
